notes:
SOURCE. English Wiktionary, read from the kaikki.org machine extraction (https://kaikki.org/dictionary/Korean), extracted 2026-08-28 from the enwiktionary dump of 2026-08-05. Every row's sourceUrl is the Wiktionary page that renders the transcription; the IPA is Wiktionary's own, with only its enclosing brackets removed. Nothing here was generated by a tool or a model - the repo's chinese-to-pinyin / to-jyutping / es-hangul packages were not used as a source for any field.

VARIETY. Seoul / South Korean standard: Wiktionary sounds tagged SK-Standard + Seoul. North Korean readings were rejected where an entry carried both.

IPA IS SURFACE, AFTER ASSIMILATION - the specific failure being measured. Wiktionary's Korean IPA already applies the obligatory sandhi, so 한국말 is ha̠(ː)nɡuŋma̠ɭ and not a letter-by-letter *hanguk-mal. Enclosing square brackets were removed; nothing else was changed. There are no tone marks and no ASCII digits in Korean IPA.

ROMANIZATION is Revised Romanization, taken from Wiktionary's `romanization` form. RR itself already spells the assimilated surface (한국말 -> han'gungmal, 심리학 -> simnihak), so it independently corroborates the IPA.

PHONETIC HANGUL. `phoneticHangul` is Wiktionary's own phonetic-hangul respelling (한국말 -> 한(ː)궁말), present on 370 rows. It is a third independent statement of the same surface form and makes the assimilation auditable without reading IPA. Note that kaikki strips the inter-word spaces from it, so the multi-word rows read 등잔미치어둡꼬... where Wiktionary renders 등잔 미치 어둡꼬...; the jamo sequence is unchanged.

ASSIMILATION FLAGS. `assimilation: true` marks every row whose pronunciation differs from a letter-by-letter reading of the spelling - 191 of 370 rows. It was computed, not asserted, by comparing the orthographic jamo against Wiktionary's phonetic hangul. `assimilationTypes` names the processes: tensification 80, liaison 53, neutralisation 47, nasalisation 31, aspiration 25, cluster-simplification 24, n-insertion 18, h-deletion 16, lateralisation 14, vowel-change 5, palatalisation 5. "liaison" is resyllabification (이름이 -> 이르미) rather than assimilation proper; the categories that matter most for the espeak-ng failure are nasalisation (ㄱ+ㅁ -> ㅇㅁ, ㅂ+ㄴ -> ㅁㄴ), lateralisation (ㄴ+ㄹ -> ㄹㄹ, ㄹ -> ㄴ after ㅁ/ㅇ), tensification, aspiration across ㅎ, and palatalisation (같이 -> 가치). The classifier is a convenience field; the authoritative statement is `ipa` plus `phoneticHangul`.

NARROWNESS - READ THIS BEFORE SCORING. Wiktionary's Korean IPA is a narrow phonetic transcription, not a broad phonemic one, and a naive string comparison will punish a correct answer. It uses: the retracted/lowered diacritics a̠ e̞ o̞ ʌ̹ (and ɘ for long 어); ɭ for coda ㄹ and ʎ before ㅣ/j, where a broad transcription writes l; sʰ for ㅅ; ɦ, ɸʷ, βʷ, ç, ʝ as the positional allophones of ㅎ (회사 = ɸwe̞(ː)sʰa̠); cç for ㄱ before ㅣ; ʃʰɥ in 쉽다; ɲ before ㅣ/j; tie bars on affricates (t͡ɕ, d͡ʑ); a leading ˈ on 49 rows, which marks the accentual phrase rather than lexical stress (Korean has none); and PARENTHESISED OPTIONAL LENGTH (ː), as in ha̠(ː)nɡuŋma̠ɭ, on 78 rows. A scorer should fold a̠->a, e̞->e, o̞->o, ʌ̹->ʌ, ɭ/ʎ->l, sʰ->s, strip ˈ and the tie bars, and either strip or ignore "(ː)". The parentheses are Wiktionary's notation for optional vowel length and are not enclosing delimiters.

SYMBOL INVENTORY vs Help:IPA/Korean (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Korean). The consonant series match the key (plain / tense p͈ t͈ k͈ ts͈ tɕ͈ / aspirated pʰ tʰ kʰ tsʰ tɕʰ, unreleased p̚ t̚ k̚, ɾ vs ɭ, ŋ). Everything listed under NARROWNESS above is Wiktionary detail beyond the key.

VALIDATION. Rows pass: zero ASCII digits, no enclosing / or [ ], at least one vowel, deduplicated on `text`, and a Revised Romanization present. Rows whose kaikki romanization field was truncated to a bare particle (a known extraction artefact, e.g. "-reul") were dropped, as were headwords containing digits.

SELECTION. Word tier: mine - TOPIK 1-2 core vocabulary chosen to load every major sandhi class deliberately (한국말 국물 학년 for ㄱ+nasal, 감사합니다 십니다 for ㅂ+ㄴ, 신라 연락 편리 실내 난로 for ㄴ+ㄹ, 심리학 정리 종로 대통령 for ㄹ after ㅁ/ㅇ, 학교 식당 잡지 for tensification, 축하 백화점 입학 for ㅎ aspiration, 같이 굳이 해돋이 for palatalisation, 옷 밖 꽃 앞 밭 부엌 무릎 for coda neutralisation, 꽃잎 색연필 for ㄴ-insertion). Sentence tier: 55 hand-picked plus 45 harvested. Transcriptions are never mine.

MULTIPLE READINGS. Korean homographs differ in VOWEL LENGTH, which Revised Romanization does not write - so the two readings share a romanization and differ only in the IPA: 눈 [nun] "eye" vs [nu(ː)n] "snow", 말 [ma̠(ː)ɭ] "speech" vs [ma̠ɭ] "horse", 사과 [sʰa̠ɡwa̠] "apple" vs [ˈsʰa̠(ː)ɡwa̠] "apology", 밤, 배, 벌, 굴, 성인, 전기, 부자. 41 rows carry `ipaAlternatives`, with `romanizationAlternatives` and `phoneticHangulAlternatives` positionally aligned - index 0 pairs with index 0. `romanizationAlternatives` therefore often repeats `romanization` verbatim; that is correct rather than a defect, and it is exactly why these are the sharpest rows in the set - an engine that ignores vowel length cannot be caught by romanization here, only by the IPA. `phoneticHangulAlternatives` shows the same contrast in hangul (눈 vs 눈(ː)). Across the curated candidate lists 23 headwords had more than one reading and were previously truncated to one; none were rejected for it. Bound morphemes (RR written -bal, mal-) and surname entries that merely repeat an existing reading are excluded. The irregular ㄼ / ㄺ clusters are included deliberately as single-reading rows, because the reduction is unpredictable and splits both ways: 밟다 [ˈpa̠(ː)p̚t͈a̠] keeps ㅂ while 넓다 [nʌ̹ɭt͈a̠] keeps ㄹ.

SENTENCE TIER, AND WHERE IT STOPS. Wiktionary's Korean usage examples carry RR but no IPA, so the sentence tier is multi-word headword entries - phrases, proverbs and multi-word verb expressions - which do get whole-expression IPA and therefore show assimilation ACROSS word boundaries: 새해 복 많이 받으세요 is sʰɛɦɛ po̞ŋma̠ni pa̠dɯsʰe̞jo (복 많이 -> 봉마니), and 밤말은 쥐가 듣고 낮말은 새가 듣는다 shows 낮말 -> 난말 and 듣는다 -> 든는다. This is the binding constraint of the three languages: the pool of attested Korean multi-word / phrase entries with both IPA and RR is 886 after excluding proper names, of which roughly 130 are phrase or proverb entries and the rest are multi-word verb and noun expressions. 100 rows were reachable; a materially larger Korean sentence tier would need a source other than Wiktionary.
